Jacqueline Scholl 2024, based on Legrand 2022 (and their R code)

Note: to preprocess the heart rate signal, i.e. look for outliers, we used the systole package from LEgrand and Allen (2022) in Python and upload the results here.

# Packages, loading
Load the raw data, but also the pre-processed data, so that we can compare our and their results

Data columns:

- Condition: 'Less' or 'More',refers to response BPM being smaller than ('less') listenBPM
- Modality: Extero or Intero, refers to two task conditoins, comparing either the heart beat or external sounds
- Decision: 'Less' or 'More', refers to participants ratings
- DecisionRT
- Confidence: rating of confidence in the response
- ConfidenceRT
- ResponseCorrect: whether Decision and Condition match
- listenBPM and responseBPM: the beats per minute of the sound/heart in the 'listening' and 'comparing' intervals


Columns with only the sae entry for each:
- TrialType?? all are 'psi'
- StairCond, all 'psi'

From their model?:
- Alpha
- EstimatedThreshold
- EstimatedSlope

From the paper:
- rejecting trials with responses < 100ms
- rejecting trials with 'unreliable heartbeat signal', i.e. absolute deviation around the median rule (Leys et al. 2013), i.e. outliers in average heart rate or standard deviation of pulse-to-pulse interval an outlier

In the code from the original paper, they're R files are in docs>source>examples>R

# Illustrations
To look at data quality:
- number of trials removed based on heart rate measure or on RT
- average % accuracy

To understand the task (for this just using the good data:
- difference between listen and response BPM; separately for the two modalities
- % choice against difference listen and response (for the two modalities separately). If we were to fit hierarchical models, we could get that automatically
- histogram of decision RTs
- histogram of confidence ratings, for the two conditions
- confidence against choice difficulty



# Fit models for each person, for each session, for each condition:
- choice (more/less) ~ stimulus difficulty + ? stimulus per se + ? response repetition bias?
- confidence: they have the relationship between confidence and ground truth accuracy


Key models for the paper: choice and confidence
##Fit
```{r}
results.indivModalities=data.frame()
results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot=data.frame()
results.allModalities=data.frame()
cardio.scaled=cardio %>% dplyr::ungroup() %>% dplyr::mutate_at(vars(c('DV_ResponseMinListen','easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs','DecisionRT','Confidence')),scale)
for (isub in unique(cardio$ID)){
  dft=cardio.scaled %>% dplyr::filter(ID==isub) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Decision = recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0),
                  ResponseCorrect = recode(ResponseCorrect,'True'=1,'False'=0))
  for (isess in unique(dft$session)){
    for (imod in unique(dft$Modality)){
      df= dft %>% dplyr::filter(session==isess & Modality==imod)
      # Separately for each condition
      glms=list()
      glms$dec = glm(Decision~ DV_ResponseMinListen,data=df,family='binomial')
     # glms$acc = glm(ResponseCorrect~ easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs,data=df,family='binomial')
     # glms$conf= lm(Confidence ~ easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs+ResponseCorrect+DecisionRT,data=df)
      glms$conf= lm(Confidence ~ easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs,data=df)
      for (ireg in names(glms)){
        t=as.data.frame(summary(glms[[ireg]])$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,session=isess,Modality=imod,regression=ireg)
        results.indivModalities=bind_rows(results.indivModalities,t)
      }
      # For the plot also without scaling
      df.notscaled= cardio %>%  dplyr::filter(ID==isub & session==isess & Modality==imod) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(Decision = recode(Decision,'More'=1,'Less'=0))
      glm.dec.notScaled= glm(Decision~DV_ResponseMinListen,data=df.notscaled,family='binomial')
      t=as.data.frame(summary(glm.dec.notScaled)$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,session=isess,Modality=imod,regression='dec')
      results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot = bind_rows(results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot,t)
    }
    
    # Combining conditions
    df= dft %>% dplyr::filter(session==isess)
    glms=list()
    glms$dec= glm(Decision~ DV_ResponseMinListen*Modality,data=df,family='binomial')
    #glms$acc= glm(ResponseCorrect~ DV_ResponseMinListen*Modality,data=df,family='binomial')
    glms$conf= lm(Confidence ~ (easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs+ResponseCorrect+DecisionRT)*Modality,data=df)
    for (ireg in names(glms)){
        t=as.data.frame(summary(glms[[ireg]])$coefficients) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column() %>%
          dplyr::mutate(ID=isub,session=isess,regression=ireg)
        results.allModalities=bind_rows(results.allModalities,t)
      }
  }
}

results.indivModalities=results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::mutate(rowname=recode(rowname,`(Intercept)` = 'Intercept')) %>%
  left_join(.,med.data,by='ID')
write.csv(results.indivModalities,file=file.path(paths$base.path,'Data_preprocessed','Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegression.csv'))
t= results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression=='dec') %>% dplyr::select(-`Std. Error`,-`z value`,-`t value`,-`Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','rowname','order'),values_from='Estimate',names_from=c('session','Modality')) %>% #'Age','Sex',
    dplyr::mutate(Extero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Extero-NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Intero-NDM_Intero)
write.csv(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=="DV_ResponseMinListen"),file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegressio_dec_DVResponseMinListen.csv'))
write.csv(t %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=="Intercept")%>%
            dplyr::mutate(Intero_absCDM_m_absNDM=abs(CDM_Intero)-abs(NDM_Intero)),
          file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_Regression_withinSubjRegressio_dec_absIntercept.csv'))

results.allModalities  =results.allModalities %>% dplyr::mutate(rowname=recode(rowname,`(Intercept)` = 'Intercept'))%>%
  left_join(.,med.data,by='ID')
```

##Analyse the regression weights
Bayes factors to be done with JASP
```{r}
session.comparisons=data.frame()
all.bfs=data.frame()

for (itype in c('conf','dec')){ 
# make the difference CDM min NDM
  dft = results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression==itype) %>% dplyr::select(-`Std. Error`,-`z value`,-`t value`,-`Pr(>|t|)`) %>%
    pivot_wider(.,id_cols=c('ID','rowname','order'),values_from='Estimate',names_from=c('session','Modality')) %>% #'Age','Sex',
    dplyr::mutate(Extero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Extero-NDM_Extero,
                  Intero_CDMmNDM = CDM_Intero-NDM_Intero)
  
  
  # when itype is dec, let's also test the absolute
  if (itype=='dec'){
    t= dft %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='Intercept') %>%
      dplyr::mutate(rowname=recode(rowname,Intercept="Intercept.abs"),
                    Intero_CDMmNDM=abs(CDM_Intero)-abs(NDM_Intero),
                    Extero_CDMmNDM=abs(CDM_Extero)-abs(NDM_Extero))
    dft=bind_rows(dft,t)
  }
  for (ibeta in unique(dft$rowname)){
    
    for (imodality in c('Intero','Extero')){
      df = dft %>% dplyr::filter(rowname==ibeta) %>% dplyr::select(order,contains(imodality))
      # compute for each of CDM and NDM a t-test against zero (one-sample,two-sided)
      main.effects= df %>%  dplyr::select(-contains('CDMmNDM')) %>%
        pivot_longer(cols=contains(imodality),names_to='session',values_to='value') %>%
        dplyr::group_by(session) %>% dplyr::summarize(p.value.session.mainEffect=t.test(value,mu=0)$p.value) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(rowname=ibeta,Modality=imodality,type=itype) %>% dplyr::select(session,p.value.session.mainEffect) %>%
        pivot_wider(.,names_from=session,values_from=p.value.session.mainEffect,names_prefix = 'p.value.session.mainEffect__') %>%
        # from the column name remove imodality
        dplyr::rename_all(~str_remove(.,imodality))
      # Regression
      this.lm= lm(formula=paste0(imodality,'_CDMmNDM~ 1+order'),data=df) 
      stats.summary=as.data.frame(summary(this.lm)$coefficients) %>% rownames_to_column(var='group.level.reg') %>% 
        # recode group.level.reg (Intercept) with NDM min CDM
        dplyr::mutate(group.level.reg=recode(group.level.reg,`(Intercept)`='NDMminCDM')) %>% 
        pivot_wider(names_from=group.level.reg,values_from=c('Estimate','Std. Error','t value','Pr(>|t|)'),names_sep='__')
      
      # # Computing a Bayes Factor for the absence of an effect
      # BFs.file = file.path(paths$base.path,'Data_preprocessed','Cardio_regressions',paste0('BFs_',itype,'_',ibeta,'_',imodality,'.RData'))
      # if (!file.exists(BFs.file)){
      #   model1.string=paste0(imodality,'_CDMmNDM~0+Intercept')
      #   model2.string=paste0(imodality,'_CDMmNDM~0')
      #   model3.string=paste0(imodality,'_CDMmNDM~0+Intercept+order') # I think it was not a good idea to include order - same problem as for the other models
      #   priors=c(1)
      #   
      #   # add a reasonable prior for that specific regressor
      #   if (ibeta=='Intercept.abs'){
      #     var.reg.weights= results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(Modality==imodality & regression==itype & rowname=="Intercept")%>% dplyr::group_by(rowname,session) %>%

      #   mean.by.cohensd0.5= 0.5*sqrt(var.reg.weights%>%dplyr::filter(session=='CDM') %>% pull(Var) + var.reg.weights%>%dplyr::filter(session=='NDM') %>% pull(Var))
      #   
      #   #priors=c(priors,max.reg.weights  %>% pull(max.abs)*0.5/(0.64)) #0.5: 50% effect size; Z=0.64: well inside, 25% percentile [i.e. 50% total]
```

# Figures for the paper
## Decision curves with predictions

We can use the regression weights created above to create a predicted value of % choice for each person for each value
```{r}
x=seq(-51,51,1)
predictions=data.frame()
for (isub in unique(results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot$ID)){
  for (isess in c('NDM','CDM')){
    for (imod in c('Intero','Extero')){
      pars = results.indivModalities.notScaled.forPlot %>% dplyr::filter(ID==isub & session==isess & regression=='dec' & Modality==imod) %>% 
        dplyr::select(rowname,Estimate) %>%pivot_wider(.,values_from=Estimate,names_from=rowname)
      y = 1/(1+exp(-(pars$`(Intercept)`+x*pars$DV_ResponseMinListen)))
      predictions=rbind(predictions,
                        data.frame(DV_ResponseMinListen=x,perc.choice.predicted=y,ID=isub,session=isess,Modality=imod))
    }
  }
}

```

For each modality, for each session, plot the choice curves with predicted values (copying again code from above to create binned choices, but plotting with ggplot for more flexibility)
```{r}
bins = data.frame(low=quantile(c(min(cardio$DV_ResponseMinListen)-0.5,cardio$DV_ResponseMinListen), probs = seq(0,0.9,0.1)), # to make sure we get the edges with the later rules
                  high=quantile(c(max(cardio$DV_ResponseMinListen)+0.5,cardio$DV_ResponseMinListen), probs = seq(0.1,1,0.1))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label=(low+high)/2)
df.real= cardio  %>%
  dplyr::select(Condition,Modality,Decision,DecisionRT,Confidence,ConfidenceRT,ResponseCorrect,ID,session, DV_ResponseMinListen) %>%
  fuzzy_left_join(.,bins,by=c('DV_ResponseMinListen'='low','DV_ResponseMinListen'='high'),
                  match_fun = list(`>=`, `<`)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ID,Modality,label,session) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(bin=label) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(perc.choice= sum(Decision=='More')/n()) %>% dplyr::ungroup() 
df.real.summary= df.real%>% dplyr::group_by(Modality,session,bin) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mChoice=mean(perc.choice),perc.choice.sd=sd(perc.choice),n=n(),seChoice=perc.choice.sd/sqrt(n))

dodge_width=0.5

df.real.this=df.real %>%
```

## Regression weights
For decision: 
- Intercept
- absolute intercept
- decision value
For confidence:
- all regression weights (+intercept)
Each split for the two groups. And split for intero/extero. Tim should add the statistics manually (nothing significant).
So the figure would be:
```{r}
# Create a figure with the regression weights from the data frame results.indivModalities. In the figure, there are 4 separate subplots, for each combination of Modality (Extero or Intero) and regression (dec or conf, ignoring acc). In each subplot, we want to show all regression weights (in the column 'rowname'), separately for each session (CDM or NDM). The regression weights should be plotted as mean and standard deviations. The figure should be saved as a pdf file in the folder paths$figures, with the name Interoception_RegressionWeights.pdf. The figure should have a title, and the x-axis should be labeled 'Regression weight'. The y-axis should be labeled 'Regression weight'. The x-axis should be rotated by 45 degrees. The colors should be the same as in the previous figure. 
plots=list()
df=results.indivModalities %>% dplyr::filter(regression %in% c('dec','conf')) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(rowname=recode(rowname,`(Intercept)` = 'Intercept',
                DV_ResponseMinListen="Stimulus difference",easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs="Stimulus easiness",
                ResponseCorrect="Correct response",DecisionRT="RT (decision)"))

for (imod in c('Intero','Extero')){
  for (ireg in c('dec','conf')){
    df.this=df %>% dplyr::filter(Modality==imod,regression==ireg)
    if (ireg=='dec'){
      t= df.this %>% dplyr::filter(rowname=='Intercept') %>%
        dplyr::mutate(rowname=recode(rowname,Intercept="Intercept.abs"),
                      Estimate=abs(Estimate))
      df.this=bind_rows(df.this,t) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(rowname=factor(rowname,ordered=T,levels=c('Stimulus difference','Intercept.abs','Intercept')))
    } else if (ireg=='conf'){
      df.this=df.this %>% dplyr::mutate(rowname=factor(rowname,ordered=T,levels=c('Stimulus easiness','Intercept')))
    }
    # plots[[paste0(imod,'_',ireg)]]=ggerrorplot(df.this,x='rowname',y='Estimate',color='session',ylab='Regression weights',add='jitter',
    #                                            add.params = list(size = 0.3),title='',size=0.4,desc_stat='mean_se') +
    #   rotate_x_text(45)+
    #   # add a horizontal line at y=0
    #   geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype='dashed',color='black')+
    #   # change the color of session=NDM to blue and CDM to red
    #   scale_color_manual(values=c('CDM'='red','NDM'='blue'))+
    #   # remove the ylabel
    #   theme(axis.title.x=element_blank())
    
      
      jitterVal.abs=0.2
      df.this=df.this%>%dplyr::mutate(jitterVal=case_when(session=='CDM' ~ -jitterVal.abs,
                                                          T ~ jitterVal.abs),
                                      jitterVal=rnorm(nrow(df.this),mean=jitterVal,sd=0.05))
      summaryData = df.this %>%
        group_by(rowname, session) %>%
        summarise(meanEstimate = mean(Estimate)
                  , jitterVal = mean(jitterVal),
                  sdEstimate=sd(Estimate),
                  n=n(),
                  se = sdEstimate/sqrt(n)) %>%
        mutate(xmin = as.numeric(rowname)+jitterVal, #-0.04
               xend = as.numeric(rowname)+jitterVal) #+0.04)

      plots[[paste0(imod,'_',ireg)]]=ggplot(df.this, aes(x=as.numeric(rowname)+jitterVal, y=Estimate, group=ID)) +
        geom_point(size=1, aes(colour=session), alpha=0.7)+
        geom_line(size=1, alpha=0.1)+
        #scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 7.5), breaks=seq(0,7,by=1))+ 
        scale_colour_manual(values=c('CDM'='blue','NDM'='red'))+
        xlab('Regressor') +
        ggtitle('')+
        scale_x_continuous(limits=(c(0.5, 3.5)), breaks = seq(1,length(levels(df.this$rowname)),1)-0.1 , labels = levels(df.this$rowname))+
        ylab('Regression weights') +
        guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))) +
        geom_point(data=summaryData,   size=2,aes(x=xmin,y=meanEstimate,color=session,group=NA))+
        geom_errorbar(data=summaryData,aes(x=xmin,y=meanEstimate,ymin=meanEstimate-se,ymax=meanEstimate+se,color=session,group=NA))+
        
        theme_bw()
      
  }
}
# Arrange the 4 plots of the list plots into a single figure with the function ggarrange. The plots should be arranged in 2 rows and 2 columns. The labels of the subplots should be 'A) Intero - Decision', 'B) Intero - Confidence', 'C) Extero - Decision', and 'D) Extero - Confidence'. The figure should have a title 'Regression weights'. The x-axis of the figure should have no label. The y-axis of the figure should be labeled 'Regression weight'. The x-axis of the figure should be rotated by 90 degrees. The figure should be saved as a pdf file in the folder paths$figures, with the name Interoception_RegressionWeights.pdf. There should be a shared legend across the 4 subplots.
figure=ggarrange(plots$Intero_dec,plots$Intero_conf,plots$Extero_dec,plots$Extero_conf,nrow=2,ncol=2,
          labels=c('A Intero - Decision','B Intero - Confidence','C Extero - Decision','D Extero - Confidence'),
          common.legend=T,
          # left align the labels
          hjust=0)

ggexport(figure,filename=file.path(paths$figures,'Interoception_RegressionWeights.tiff'),
         width=9*400,height=7*400,res=400)

  


```


#Print the results as tables for main text and supplements
```{r}
session.comparisons=read.csv(file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_NDMCDMcomparisons_fitSingleSub.csv'))
# main text: Intero/Extero, decision/confidence, against zero (CDM and NDM separately), comparing NDM vs CDM (estimate (se.); p-value, BF), order effects
main=session.comparisons %>% 
  dplyr::select(Modality,analysis.type,Subject.level.regression.weight,contains('.mainEffect'),
                Estimate__NDMminCDM,Std..Error__NDMminCDM,Pr...t..__NDMminCDM,Estimate__orderNDM.first,Std..Error__orderNDM.first,Pr...t..__orderNDM.first) %>%  #BF.mean.customSD
  dplyr::mutate("NDM vs CDM, mean(s.e.)"=paste0(round(Estimate__NDMminCDM,digits=2),' (',round(Std..Error__NDMminCDM,digits=1),')'),
                "NDM vs CDM (p)"=case_when(Pr...t..__NDMminCDM<0.01 ~ round(Pr...t..__NDMminCDM,digits=3),
                                T ~ round(Pr...t..__NDMminCDM,digits=2)),
                #"BF NDM vs CDM ==0"= round(BF.mean.customSD,digits=1),
                "Order [NDM first], mean(s.e.)" =paste0(round(Estimate__orderNDM.first,digits=2),' (',round(Std..Error__orderNDM.first,digits=1),')'),
                "Order [NDM first] (p)" = case_when(Pr...t..__orderNDM.first<0.01 ~ round(Pr...t..__orderNDM.first,digits=3),
                                T ~ round(Pr...t..__orderNDM.first,digits=2)),
                p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_= case_when(p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_<0.001 ~ '<0.001',
                                                            p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_<0.01 ~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,digits=3)),
                                                            T~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,digits=2))),
                p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_= case_when(p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_ < 0.001 ~ '<0.001',
                                                            p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_<0.01 ~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_,digits=3)),
                                                            T~ as.character(round(p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_,digits=2)))) %>%
  dplyr::rename("CDM (p, one-sample)"=p.value.session.mainEffect__CDM_,
                "NDM (p, one-sample)"=p.value.session.mainEffect__NDM_)%>%
  dplyr::select(-contains('Pr...'),-contains('Estimate__'),-contains('Std..Error'),-contains('p.value.session.main')) %>% #,-BF.mean.customSD) %>%
  # sort the data frame frist by Modality, then by analysis.type, then by Subject.level.regression.weight
  dplyr::arrange(desc(Modality)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Subject.level.regression.weight=recode(Subject.level.regression.weight,DV_ResponseMinListen="Stimulus difference",easiness_ResponseMinListen.abs="Stimulus easiness",ResponseCorrect="Correct response",DecisionRT="RT (decision)"))
  # I'm not very confident in the Bayes factors, let's remove them
  #dplyr::select(-`BF NDM vs CDM ==0`)

write.csv(main,file=file.path(paths$stats,'Interoception_NDMCDMcomparisons_mainText.csv'))
```
